chunk-001:c003.proposition: Science's omission of God from ordinary mechanisms does not establish atheism, because the intelligibility and origins of the universe remain deeper questions and scientism is self-defeating.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of an earlier opposing move, Lennox's distinction between scientific mechanisms and deeper questions of intelligibility and origins positively limits what methodological science can establish metaphysically.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: The effectiveness of mathematics in describing the physical universe is expected if a divine mind grounds both cosmic rationality and human rational capacities, but is surprising under naturalism.

orphanFallback.rationale: Lennox presents mathematical effectiveness as direct positive evidence for a common divine source of the universe's order and the rational capacities of human minds.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Christian faith is an evidence-based commitment rather than a reasonless leap, and asking who created God misconstrues the biblical God as a created entity.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone constructive claim, the move defines Christian faith as evidence-based and states that creator regress applies to created beings rather than to the uncreated God Lennox describes.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Christian commitment rests on cumulative evidence comprising resurrection testimony, intellectual inference, personally testable promises of Christ, and observed transformation in lived experience.

orphanFallback.rationale: The cited historical, inferential, experiential, and transformative considerations independently constitute Lennox's positive cumulative account of the grounds for Christian faith.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: The Cana account reports an actual divine miracle that adds an event without violating natural law and whose physical occurrence reveals Jesus' identity and redemptive purpose.

orphanFallback.rationale: Lennox positively presents Cana as a real sign whose occurrence is coherent with natural regularity and whose symbolism of joy and purification discloses Jesus' identity and purpose.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c04.proposition: The Gospel narrative gains evidential and theological power when its meaning rests on real signs that progressively reveal Christ as the Son of God and ground belief in him.

orphanFallback.rationale: Without relying on an earlier objection, Lennox offers historical reality as the positive basis that strengthens the Gospel narrative and makes its signs evidence of Christ's identity.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c05.proposition: Atheism removes objective good and evil without removing suffering, whereas the cross depicts divine participation in suffering and the resurrection supplies grounds for hope.

orphanFallback.rationale: The cross and resurrection independently form Lennox's constructive Christian account of a God who enters suffering and provides hope rather than merely leaving suffering unexplained.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c10.proposition: A world capable of freely chosen love must permit rebellion, while preventing moral evil through complete determinism would eliminate genuinely human relationships.

orphanFallback.rationale: Lennox's contrast between free persons and deterministic robots independently supplies a positive free-will account of why the possibility of wrongdoing accompanies the possibility of love.
